t: Introduction and overview — A-10 Thunderbolt II
name: Introduction and overview — A-10 Thunderbolt II — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — A-10 Thunderbolt II
description: Introduction and overview of the A-10 Thunderbolt II: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The A-10 Thunderbolt II, nicknamed Warthog, is a twin-engine close-air-support aircraft built by Fairchild Republic, entering service in 1977. It was designed around the 30 mm GAU-8 Avenger rotary cannon, one of the most powerful aircraft guns ever flown. 716 were built; the type's armor, redundancy, and loiter time kept it in service for decades. Baseline facts: Twin-engine close-air-support aircraft; USAF service from 1977; 716 built by Fairchild Republic..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: A-10 Thunderbolt II: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Twin-engine close-air-support aircraft; USAF service from 1977; 716 built by Fairchild Republic.
Key figure: GAU-8 Avenger 30 mm cannon; titanium armor bathtub; two General Electric TF34 turbofans.
